calculators.title: HEART score

options.label: Significant ST deviation, not known old
3 or more, or known atherosclerotic disease

bands.text: 0 to 3: low risk; a candidate for early discharge
4 to 6: moderate risk; observation and further evaluation
7 to 10: high risk; a candidate for urgent intervention

calculators.note: Risk factors: diabetes, smoking, hypertension, high cholesterol, obesity, a family history of coronary disease. Known atherosclerotic disease: a past MI or coronary revascularization, peripheral arterial disease, stroke. Troponin against the local assay's cutoff. The 2021 chest pain guideline calls 3 or less low risk only with initial and serial troponins below the 99th percentile (Table 8).

options: Draw a troponin and wait for it
nodes.chainStep: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first contact; blood pressure in both arms
nodes.why: The ECG sorts ST elevation from everything else, and the clock is 10 minutes from first medical contact. Take the pressure in both arms while it prints.
nodes.note: Hypotension or distended neck veins: a bedside echo looks for effusion and tamponade before the route goes on. Not in this version: tension pneumothorax (a bedside diagnosis), esophageal rupture, shock, presentations 12 to 24 hours old, a new LBBB.

orders.dose: Useful to look for other cardiac, pulmonary and thoracic causes; it does not come before the ECG

outcomes.if: ST elevation in II, III and aVF; no features of an aortic syndrome
ST elevation in another territory; no features of an aortic syndrome
Pericarditis pattern; diffuse ST elevation with PR depression, no reciprocal change
No ST elevation, no features of an aortic syndrome
Aortic syndrome features; abrupt severe chest or back pain with a pulse deficit or an arm pressure gap, a focal neurologic deficit, or a known aortic aneurysm or connective tissue disease

nodes.ask: Inferior ST elevation. Before any nitroglycerin?
options: IV morphine for the pain first
IV metoprolol before the cath lab
nodes.why: Right-sided leads look for right ventricular involvement, the inferior STEMI whose pressure falls on nitroglycerin.

orders.dose: Avoid: suspected RV infarction
Only if hypotensive with clear lungs; not stated in the ACS guideline
If hypotension persists after fluids; agent not stated in the ACS guideline

outcomes.if: Cath lab here; primary PCI within 90 minutes of first contact
Transfer within 120 minutes; no cath lab here, but transfer gets first contact to device within 120 minutes
PCI over 120 minutes away; no cath lab here, symptoms under 12 hours, no contraindication to fibrinolysis

nodes.ask: Primary PCI is reachable in time. Reperfusion?
options: Primary PCI: first contact to device 90 minutes, or 120 with a transfer
Admit and repeat the ECG in 6 hours
Bedside echo to confirm a wall motion abnormality first
nodes.chainStep: Primary PCI: first contact to device 90 minutes, or 120 with a transfer
nodes.why: Primary PCI within 90 minutes of first medical contact, or 120 when the patient must be transferred.

nodes.ask: A prior stroke or TIA rules out which P2Y12 load?
nodes.chainStep: Aspirin 162 to 325 mg chewed plus ticagrelor 180 mg (never prasugrel after a stroke or TIA), heparin for PCI, high-intensity statin
nodes.why: Prasugrel after a stroke or TIA is Class 3: Harm. Ticagrelor or prasugrel is the usual partner for aspirin when PCI is the plan.

orders.dose: 162 to 325 mg, chewed; then 75 to 100 mg daily
180 mg load; then 90 mg twice daily
No prior anticoagulant: 70 to 100 U/kg bolus, target ACT 250 to 300 s
Atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg

nodes.ask: The nearest PCI center is more than 120 minutes away. Reperfusion?
options: Transfer for primary PCI whatever the delay
Fibrinolysis, then keep her here unless the pain returns
nodes.chainStep: Fibrinolysis now, then immediate transfer for angiography at 2 to 24 hours
nodes.why: With PCI more than 120 minutes from first contact and symptoms under 12 hours, give a fibrinolytic, then transfer at once for angiography at 2 to 24 hours. Check the absolute contraindications first: a suspected aortic dissection is one.

nodes.chainStep: Tenecteplase as one IV bolus by weight (40 mg at 70 to 79 kg), with aspirin, clopidogrel and enoxaparin
nodes.why: One weight-based IV bolus: 30 mg under 60 kg, 35 mg for 60 to 69, 40 mg for 70 to 79, 45 mg for 80 to 89, 50 mg for 90 kg and over.

orders.dose: Single IV bolus by weight: 30, 35, 40, 45 or 50 mg
162 to 325 mg, chewed
300 mg load under 75 years, then 75 mg daily; 75 mg daily with no load in older patients
orders.note: The guideline's Table 7 puts age 75 itself in the load group; its text puts it in the no-load group.

orders.dose: Under 75 years: 30 mg IV, then 15 minutes later 1 mg/kg SC every 12 h (max 100 mg for the first 2 doses). 75 and over: 0.75 mg/kg SC every 12 h, no bolus (max 75 mg for the first 2 doses). Continue for the hospital stay, up to 8 days, or until revascularization
Immediately; angiography at 2 to 24 hours
Immediate angiography and rescue PCI if ST elevation resolves less than 50% (anterior) or 70% (inferior), symptoms persist, or she becomes unstable

options: hs-troponin now and again at 1 to 2 hours
Conventional troponin now and again at 1 hour
nodes.chainStep: hs-troponin now and again at 1 to 2 hours
nodes.why: A high-sensitivity troponin now and again at 1 to 2 hours; thresholds are specific to the assay. Fibrinolysis without ST elevation brings harm and no benefit, except a true posterior STEMI: ST depression in V1 to V3 calls for V7 to V9.

outcomes.if: Above the 99th percentile with a rise or fall
Low risk; troponin negative and HEART 3 or less, or one undetectable draw with symptoms 3 or more hours before arrival and a normal ECG

orders.dose: Recommended once a high decision pathway score designates the patient high risk

nodes.chainStep: Aspirin, heparin 60 IU/kg (max 4,000) then 12 IU/kg/h (max 1,000), nitrates for pain, high-intensity statin; angiography timed by risk
nodes.why: Weight based with caps, aPTT 60 to 80 seconds. When no early invasive approach is planned, enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 hours or fondaparinux are the alternatives.

orders.dose: 162 to 325 mg, chewed; then 75 to 100 mg daily
180 mg load, then 90 mg twice daily. Angiography within 24 hours: load at PCI. Upstream only when angiography is expected after 24 hours (Class 2b) or no invasive plan

orders.item: Enoxaparin (instead of heparin when no early invasive approach is planned)
orders.dose: 1 mg/kg SC every 12 h; 1 mg/kg SC every 24 h if CrCl under 30
0.3 to 0.4 mg SL every 5 min, up to 3 doses; SBP 90 or more; no avanafil in 12 h, sildenafil or vardenafil in 24 h, tadalafil in 48 h
Oral, within 24 hours if no contraindication; the guideline names no agent or dose
Atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg

Under 2 hours if unstable (shock, heart failure, refractory angina, VT or VF); under 24 hours if high risk (GRACE over 140, a steeply rising troponin despite treatment, ongoing dynamic ST changes); before discharge, under 72 hours, if intermediate risk

nodes.ask: Low HEART score, both troponins below the 99th percentile. Disposition?
options: Discharge home without urgent cardiac testing
nodes.chainStep: Discharge home without urgent cardiac testing
nodes.why: A HEART score of 3 or less with negative troponins marks a 30-day risk under 1%: home without admission or urgent testing. A single undetectable hs-troponin also rules out injury when symptoms began 3 or more hours before arrival and the ECG is normal.
nodes.note: Table 6 of the same guideline writes the HEART low-risk cut as under 3; Table 8 and the HEART Pathway write 3 or less. This case scores 0, low on either cut. Pulmonary embolism is not handled in this version: weigh it by pretest probability before discharge.

nodes.ask: Concern for an aortic syndrome. Next?
options: CT angiography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
Chest x-ray to rule it out
D-dimer first; CT only if it is raised
nodes.chainStep: CT angiography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
nodes.why: CT angiography first. A plain chest x-ray is neither sensitive nor specific enough to rule out an acute aortic syndrome, and a suspected dissection is an absolute contraindication to fibrinolysis.

orders.dose: Emergency surgery
Medical therapy in the ICU; when to intervene is not yet extracted

options: IV beta blocker (esmolol, metoprolol or labetalol)
IV nicardipine to reach a systolic under 120 first
nodes.chainStep: IV beta blocker first to a heart rate of 60 to 80, then a vasodilator to a systolic under 120; arterial line in the ICU
nodes.why: Rate first, then pressure: a vasodilator is avoided as the initial drug and added only after the beta blocker.

orders.dose: Systolic under 120 and heart rate 60 to 80
Agents named; no dose stated in the guideline. If a beta blocker cannot be used: IV verapamil or diltiazem for rate (Class 2a)
Only after the beta blocker
Arterial line, ICU
IV opioids
Absolute contraindication

nodes.summary: Diffuse ST elevation with PR depression is the ECG hallmark of pericarditis, a STEMI mimic: no cath lab and no fibrinolytic. Its workup and treatment are not in this pathway's sources yet.
Inferior STEMI: primary PCI, aspirin plus ticagrelor, heparin, high-intensity statin; no nitroglycerin when the right ventricle is involved.
STEMI far from PCI: tenecteplase by weight, aspirin, clopidogrel and enoxaparin, immediate transfer; rescue PCI at once if reperfusion fails, otherwise angiography at 2 to 24 hours.

NSTEMI: aspirin, heparin, nitrates for pain, a high-intensity statin, an oral beta blocker within 24 hours, and angiography timed by risk; the P2Y12 load waits for PCI when angiography is within 24 hours.
Low risk: home without admission or urgent cardiac testing.
Acute aortic syndrome: CT angiography, beta blocker first, systolic under 120 and heart rate 60 to 80; type A to surgery; never a fibrinolytic.
Troponin negative but HEART 4 to 6: intermediate risk, where further diagnostic testing may be indicated. Which test is not yet in this pathway.
Troponin negative but HEART 7 or more: a high decision pathway score makes this high risk for short-term MACE, and invasive coronary angiography is recommended.

cases.label: Inferior STEMI, right ventricle involved
cases.vignette: 58-year-old man, 40 minutes of substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm, diaphoretic. BP 148/90, HR 96, SpO2 97%. Cath lab on site.

results.first_look: ECG: 2 mm ST elevation in II, III and aVF. Arm pressures equal, no back pain.
results.pci_access: The interventional team can have him on the table within the hour.

cases.label: STEMI, two hours from a cath lab
cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman at a rural emergency department, 2 hours of crushing chest pressure. BP 152/88, HR 88. Weight 72 kg. No prior intracranial bleed or stroke, no head trauma, no bleeding, no recent surgery.

results.first_look: ECG: 3 mm ST elevation in II, III and aVF. Arm pressures equal, no back pain.
results.pci_access: The nearest PCI center is two and a half hours away by road.

cases.label: Anterior STEMI, transfer for PCI
cases.vignette: 52-year-old man at a community hospital without a cath lab, 1 hour of chest pain. BP 138/86, HR 92. The PCI center is 40 minutes away.

results.first_look: ECG: 3 mm ST elevation in V1 to V4. Arm pressures equal, no back pain.
results.pci_access: The receiving team can open the artery within 110 minutes of first contact.

cases.label: NSTEMI
cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with diabetes, 3 hours of chest pressure at rest that eased before arrival. BP 142/84, HR 90.

results.first_look: ECG: 1 mm ST depression in V4 to V6, no ST elevation. Arm pressures equal.
results.trop_result: hs-troponin above the 99th percentile at 0 hours and higher at 1 hour.

cases.label: Low-risk chest pain
cases.vignette: 34-year-old woman, a sharp left chest pain that began while lifting, 4 hours before arrival, and has settled. No risk factors, no estrogen use, no leg swelling, no recent surgery or travel. BP 118/72, HR 74, SpO2 99%.

results.first_look: ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic change. Arm pressures equal.
results.trop_result: hs-troponin undetectable at 0 hours and at 2 hours.

cases.label: Type A dissection
cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with hypertension, sudden severe chest pain that tears through to his back. BP 182/96 in the right arm, HR 108.

results.first_look: ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST elevation. Right arm 182/96, left arm 148/80.
results.aas_type: CT angiography: an intimal flap in the ascending aorta.

cases.label: Type B dissection
cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with a known descending thoracic aneurysm, sudden severe tearing pain between the shoulder blades. BP 176/98.

results.first_look: ECG: sinus rhythm, no ST elevation. Right arm 176/98, left arm 172/96; leg pulses intact.
results.aas_type: CT angiography: a flap starting beyond the left subclavian artery; the ascending aorta is spared.

cases.label: Pericarditis, the STEMI mimic
cases.vignette: 28-year-old man, a week after a cold, sharp chest pain that is worse lying flat and eases sitting forward. BP 124/76, HR 98, temperature 37.9.

results.first_look: ECG: diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression, no reciprocal ST depression.

cases.label: Troponin negative, intermediate risk
cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes and high cholesterol, 2 hours of pressure-like chest discomfort that has eased. BP 146/88, HR 80.

results.first_look: ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic change. Arm pressures equal.
results.trop_result: hs-troponin below the 99th percentile at 0 and 2 hours. HEART score 5.

cases.label: Troponin negative, high HEART
cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with a coronary stent placed 3 years ago, diabetes and hypertension, an hour of crushing exertional chest pain into the left arm that has eased. BP 150/86, HR 84.

results.first_look: ECG: left ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization change, no ST depression. Arm pressures equal.
results.trop_result: hs-troponin below the 99th percentile at 0 and 2 hours. HEART score 7.
